unresolved.finding: The entire debugging implementation is preprocessor-disabled with an explicit rewrite note, so the compiled module exposes none of its consistency-check or checksum routines.

Four active MPI routines include genmpi_distr.inc or genmpi_coll.inc, but neither include file is present anywhere in the supplied source tree, so compiling this implementation with USEMPI would fail unless the build injects undocumented external files.
A communicator-local argument error aborts MPI_COMM_WORLD rather than the passed communicator, unexpectedly terminating unrelated communicator participants.
MPI return codes are repeatedly assigned to ier/ierror but never checked, leaving datatype, collective, or point-to-point failures without local diagnostic handling.

Both column-wise send routines deallocate the contiguous send buffer aa before all outstanding MPI_Isend requests are completed, violating MPI buffer-lifetime requirements and risking corrupted transfers.
If sum(ln(1:procs)) is zero on the root, the unconditional loop has no send event that can reach its exit test and runs forever; no positive-dimension precondition is enforced.
Local size-consistency failures abort MPI_COMM_WORLD rather than the communicator supplied to the routine, potentially terminating unrelated communicator participants.
MPI return codes are stored throughout the module but never tested, so communication failures are not distinguished from valid results.
The parameter-name and array-name entry points index keys or call indextos without validating the caller-supplied index, so an out-of-range C/API index can cause an out-of-bounds access.
The scalar C getters return c_loc of an automatic local target (r0 or i0), whose lifetime ends when the function returns, leaving the caller with an invalid pointer.
getarraydimsize_c initializes its function result to -1 and never changes it to success after computing dimsize, so every successful dimension query is reported as a failure.
getparametertype_c unconditionally returns success and does not propagate whether getkey_indextype found the requested parameter.
getarraydimsize_c checks only rank < dim, so dim values of zero or less can reach the SIZE intrinsic with an invalid dimension argument.

Each nonscalar C getter returns a pointer into a saved scratch allocation that is deallocated by the next call of the same rank/type, silently invalidating previously returned data and making the API non-reentrant.

Typed getters and setters validate only that a name exists, not that its registered type and rank match the selected entry point, so a wrong API choice can dereference an unassociated arraytype component.
C array setters infer the model target shape but accept no source-buffer length, leaving no way to reject a caller buffer that is too short before copying that many elements.

Several BIND(C) query routines omit VALUE on scalar input lengths or dimensions while neighboring C entry points pass analogous inputs by value, creating an inconsistent and undocumented pointer-versus-value calling convention.
strcmp converts char_array1 into both string1 and string2, so it never compares the second input and always returns equality.

strlen and char_array_to_string unconditionally declare and scan a 1024-element input without accepting its actual length, so sequence-associated callers with shorter C buffers can be read out of bounds.
string_to_char_array does not reject or truncate input strings of length 1024 or greater, and writes the terminator at len_trim(string)+1 beyond its fixed 1024-element result.
strlen returns zero rather than MAXSTRINGLEN when no NUL byte is present, causing a full nonterminated buffer to be misreported as empty.
executestep suppresses a nonzero timestep error by skipping physics but then unconditionally increments the step count and returns success.
outputext tests the library module's stale error variable rather than receiving a status from output, and leaves its function result undefined for error values other than 0 or 1.
init passes a shared error variable through setup operations but never checks or propagates it and unconditionally returns success after output initialization.
The library exposes one saved global model state with no initialized/finalized guard, leaving repeated init, calls before init, and calls after final as undocumented lifecycle hazards.
The exported writetolog entry point is hard-coded to emit ten test messages and report success, which appears to be diagnostic scaffolding exposed as part of the shared-library ABI.

logmsg passes an arbitrary-length message directly to string_to_char_array's fixed 1024-byte result without truncation or rejection, so messages of 1024 or more nonblank characters overflow the conversion buffer.
Errors are written to XBerror.txt during execution but close_logfiles unconditionally closes that file with STATUS='DELETE', discarding the error log even after errors were recorded.
The OPEN statements have no IOSTAT handling and the subsequent error test checks only whether a unit number was available, not whether any log file was successfully opened.
progress_indicator permits dper equal to zero and then can evaluate mod(curper,dper), which is undefined for a zero divisor.
writelog_finalize divides by the timestep count n without guarding the valid lifecycle case in which finalization occurs before any execute step.
The error==6 branch reports an excessive N-direction domain count but tells the user to reduce the M-direction count.
The non-MPI rank-4 point path sizes its third dimension from t%r3 instead of t%r4, which can dereference an unassociated rank-3 component and allocates the wrong shape.
Rank-3 and rank-4 NetCDF point output passes only the single first scalar of each sampled array, so all other vertical/class dimensions remain unwritten despite being declared in the variable.
The Fortran-compatible rank-3 and rank-4 point paths read local allocatables r3 and r4 after the sampling phase instead of pointoutputs, but those temporaries are not allocated there.
Initialization and dimension errors on the output-master-only path use STOP rather than the coordinated halt routine, which can terminate one MPI rank while leaving the others blocked.
pointsvarids is not initialized, and an unsupported point-variable type merely prints a message before attributes are written through the unassigned ID.

Multiple output paths pass chartoindex results directly to indextos or mnemonic indexing without checking for -1, so an invalid configured variable can become an out-of-bounds access rather than a controlled configuration error.
Integer global variables are declared for ranks 0 through 4 during initialization, but the writer handles only ranks 0, 2, and 3, silently leaving rank-1 or rank-4 variables unwritten.

The point writer supplies no count and uses scalar actuals for multidimensional records, leaving its intended mapping between sampled array dimensions and NetCDF dimensions unclear even when the call succeeds.
The runup-gauge loop writes unit ii+par%npoints but flushes unit i+par%npoints, where i is stale from the preceding point-variable loop.
Each drifter trajectory variable declares coordinates='pointx pointy' even though those coordinate variables use the unrelated fixed points dimension rather than the drifter trajectory dimensions.
Writing legacy mean minima and maxima mutates the live accumulated arrays by replacing sentinel extremes with -999, so output changes model-owned statistics rather than formatting a copy.
Hotstart writers capture OPEN failures in ierr but never test it and proceed to write and close the unit as if the file were valid.
handle_err attempts to close module ncid even when the failing operation may be nf90_create itself, before ncid has necessarily received a valid file identifier.
pointtypes is written twice consecutively during NetCDF initialization.

Pure NetCDF initialization does not call fortoutput_init, which is the only initializer for the saved drifter record counter used by ncoutput, so NetCDF drifter output can start from an undefined record index.
output_error claims that it creates an extra diagnostic timestep, but the output call is commented out and the routine only logs the claim before halting.
check_outputvariables_allocated validates only global variables, leaving configured point and mean variables to reach later output paths without equivalent association checks.
The allocation check passes chartoindex directly to indextos without handling an unknown configured mnemonic.
Progress reporting divides by par%tstop in several expressions without guarding a zero stop time.
The output-variable error flag is broadcast only among non-output-master ranks, so the output master does not receive the validation result before its own initialization path.
With rotation disabled, the Sutot and Svtot branches compute interpolated transport scratch arrays but never copy them into x, leaving the requested output undefined.
All rank-2/3/4 gridrotate routines leave their section bounds uninitialized when row is present but nonpositive, despite the comments making only positive row values special.
The routines test only PRESENT(row) and then reference optional col unconditionally, so a caller that supplies row without col triggers an invalid absent-optional access.
gridrotate_r3 only logs mismatched horizontal shapes and then proceeds with whole-array assignments that require those shapes to conform.

Every rank-3 rotation creates five full-grid automatic 3-D scratch arrays even when the selected variable needs none or only a subset, creating a substantial stack/memory exhaustion risk for large scientific grids.
runup is explicitly marked incorrect and assigns results only where pointtypes equals 1, leaving all other elements of its returned array undefined.
Direction conversions use 270 minus the angle in degrees without normalizing the result, so rotated output can fall outside a conventional 0–360 degree range.
Local mean initialization sizes integer rank-2/3/4 variables through the real pointer components r2/r3/r4 instead of i2/i3/i4, which can dereference unassociated pointers.
Rank-4 averaging sizes its first three dimensions from t%r3 rather than t%r4, so a normal rank-4 variable can fail before accumulation begins.
The saved sine and cosine accumulators used for thetamean are never cleared by clearaverage, so each nominal averaging period includes all prior periods.
When rotation is enabled gridrotate converts thetamean to degrees, but makeaverage immediately passes those values to SIN and COS as though they were radians.

The live code stores the circular mean directly as atan2(sine,cosine) while the former packed sine/cosine representation is commented out, leaving downstream consumers that decode the packed representation incompatible.
Although initialization accepts integer rank-3 and rank-4 mean variables, makeaverage unconditionally uses real components and real rotation paths for those ranks.
Mean-variable names are converted to indices and used immediately without checking for an unknown mnemonic.
thetamean receives a circular mean but its variance, minimum, and maximum are still computed with linear angle arithmetic, which is discontinuous across the direction wrap.
The variance recurrence divides a cross term by an epsilon-substituted old mean, so cancellation near a zero mean can strongly amplify roundoff despite the nominal zero guard.
makecrossvector uses caller-supplied mg directly as a row or column index without validating it against the selected array.
The complete legacy output module is enclosed in #if 0 and retained only for reference, so none of its declared public output routines are available to a build.
BMI initialize converts the supplied configuration-file path but never uses it, so initialization silently reads the library's default input rather than the requested file.
update overwrites the executestep return code with outputext's return code, allowing a failed model step to be reported as successful.

With morfacopt enabled, current and end time are exposed in morphology-scaled time while get_time_step returns unscaled par%dt and update accepts its dt without inverse scaling, violating a single BMI time-unit contract.
Unknown variable names cause get_var_type and get_var_rank to return without initializing their output arguments or providing an error status.
set_current_time converts and dereferences the incoming C pointer without checking for C_NULL_PTR.
get_time_step invokes compute_dt with fresh local counters instead of merely returning an established step, so a query can mutate timestep state and may differ across repeated calls.
Twelve active broadcast wrappers include xmpi_bcast.inc, but that include is absent from the source tree and is not listed among the build's generated sources.
xmpi_shift_i3 calls xmpi_sendrecv with rank-3 integer sections, but the xmpi_sendrecv generic has no rank-3 integer procedure, producing no matching specific routine.
The XPREF processor-grid branch can set nmin to zero and evaluate m/nmin; Fortran does not guarantee short-circuit evaluation of the preceding nmin>4 condition.

Normal error handling aborts xmpi_comm, which excludes the output rank and is MPI_COMM_NULL on that rank, so output-rank failures can recurse or hang and compute-rank failures can strand the output process.
On compiler configurations that leave MBACKTRACE defined, the error reporter deliberately dereferences a null pointer to force a segmentation fault before orderly MPI termination.
Character broadcast sends the source's trimmed length but never checks the receiving character capacity before assigning x(i:i), so differing declared lengths can write past the receiver.
All xmpi_sendrecv wrappers use the sender's size as the receive count without verifying that recvbuf has the same number of elements.
The paired xmpi_send wrappers derive counts independently from the sender and receiver actual arrays and exchange no shape metadata, so mismatched caller shapes yield truncation or partial data.
xmpi_getrow does not validate n, prow, or b's extent before assigning a full row and communicating n elements.
Cyclic boundary handling has cases only for 0 and 1; any other value leaves out-of-range neighbor ranks in place without setting boundary flags or returning an error.
Most MPI return codes are assigned but not inspected locally, reducing diagnostic context even where a communicator error handler may run.

The non-MPI branch defines xmpirank and xmpisize instead of the subsystem's xmpi_rank and xmpi_size names and omits xomaster, xcompute, and xmpi_orank, making this module incompatible with serial consumers of the current API.

This alternative module provides only one-argument broadcasts, a processor-grid routine without cyclic input, and a zero-argument barrier, while the surrounding subsystem calls the corresponding multi-communicator/cyclic forms.
xmpi_shift_i3 passes rank-3 integer sections to xmpi_sendrecv, but that generic has no rank-3 integer procedure.
Character broadcast does not check that each receiver's character variable is at least as long as the source string before assigning x(i:i).
Sendrecv wrappers use size(sendbuf) for both send and receive counts without validating recvbuf's extent.
Processor-grid construction has no minimum local-domain check even though halo shifts subsequently index fixed positions up to four cells from each boundary.
xmpi_getrow uses n and prow directly without checking the source row length, destination extent, or processor-row range.
MPI return codes are stored throughout but never inspected and no communicator error handler is installed in this implementation.
finalize unloads the shared library without calling its exported finalize routine, skipping model cleanup, output closure, and MPI finalization.

Nonscalar getters wrap the returned address in numpy.ctypeslib.ndpointer and then call numpy.array on that ctypes pointer object, which does not expose a valid NumPy buffer and fails instead of copying the model array.
Character-parameter retrieval allocates only one c_char even though the Fortran entry point writes a full fixed-length character array into that address.
Initialization, stepping, and output discard all native return codes, so the Python API continues silently after reported model failures.
The integer scalar setter uses c_double rather than c_int and passes that address to set0dintarray, causing the Fortran side to reinterpret floating-point bytes as an integer.

ctypes c_char results are bytes and create_string_buffer requires bytes under Python 3, but the wrapper consistently compares type codes with str literals and assumes string inputs, making core parameter and array dispatch fail.
Construction changes the process-wide working directory and stores olddir but never restores it, including after finalization or a library-load failure.
A relative library path is converted to absolute only after changing into workingdir, so it is resolved against a different directory than the caller's original context.
get_parameters constructs a set of (name,value) tuples rather than the mapping implied by the method name and typical parameter API use.
Most introspection calls discard their native status codes and return default or undefined ctypes values when lookup or transfer fails.

Finalization repeatedly calls dlclose on one saved handle until a shell-based lsof probe says the path is absent, which can reuse an already-closed handle or unload a library still shared by another wrapper instance.
isloaded depends on external lsof and interpolates an unquoted absolute path into a shell pipeline, so spaces or shell metacharacters break the check and supported non-Unix platforms cannot use it.
dlclose assumes a loadable libdl plus an unversioned suffix and compares dlerror's bytes result to a str literal, so its error classification is unreliable on Python 3 and several declared platforms.
Importing the module forces DEBUG level and attaches a new stream handler without checking for an existing handler, causing duplicate or unexpectedly verbose application logging.
